answer: Unrealised gains on gold, currencies and securities are not recognised as income; they are transferred directly to revaluation accounts (balance sheet liabilities). Unrealised losses are charged to the profit and loss account (write-downs) only if at year-end they exceed previous revaluation gains accumulated in the corresponding revaluation account; they are not netted against unrealised gains on other securities, currencies or gold, and the average cost of the written-down item is reduced to the year-end exchange rate or market price. Realised gains/losses go to the P&L.

evidence.text: Unrealised gains are not recognised as income but are transferred directly to a revaluation account.
Unrealised losses are recorded in the profit and loss account if, at the year-end, they exceed previous revaluation gains accumulated in the corresponding revaluation account.
